checks.explanation: Trump's federal classified-documents case did become bogged down in extensive pretrial litigation over classified evidence and was ultimately dismissed by Judge Cannon in July 2024, never reaching trial, well within the predicted delay window.
Christie suspended his campaign on January 10, 2024, before the New Hampshire primary was even held, and never won any primary contest.

DeSantis's campaign did end in a widely-covered, embarrassing collapse (staff turnover, poor debate performances, a distant second in Iowa) before he dropped out and endorsed Trump on January 21, 2024.
The race did not narrow to Trump versus Vivek Ramaswamy; Ramaswamy dropped out January 15, 2024 after Iowa, and Nikki Haley remained Trump's main rival through Super Tuesday in March 2024.

Hunter Biden was convicted on federal gun charges in June 2024 and tax charges in September 2024, but was not incarcerated before the November 2024 election; he was pardoned by President Biden in December 2024 before any sentence was served.
Hunter Biden was not in jail by the 2024 election; he was convicted but not yet sentenced, and was pardoned in December 2024 before serving any time.
Republican-aligned super PACs and donors did fund substantial anti-Biden and anti-Hunter-Biden advertising throughout the 2024 election cycle.
Special Counsel David Weiss did move relatively quickly, securing Hunter Biden's conviction on gun charges in June 2024, well before the November election.
The Justice Department indicted Hunter Biden on federal gun charges on September 14, 2023, matching the predicted timing.

Hunter Biden's gun and tax cases were resolved via conviction, and investigations into his foreign business dealings (Burisma, China deals) produced significant public disclosure, though no direct criminal link to Joe Biden was ever clearly established or charged.
Prosecutors did take additional time and ultimately brought charges against Hunter Biden on both gun and tax matters in 2023-2024.

Trump won the 2024 election, but no evidence indicates his administration formally reopened a Hunter Biden investigation, since Weiss's prosecution had already concluded with convictions before Biden's pardon mooted further proceedings.

Biden did not make it to the general election as the active nominee (he withdrew in July 2024), but Trump did remain the Republican nominee throughout, so only half of this joint prediction proved true.

Abortion and moderate/independent voters were widely cited as significant factors in the 2024 election, though the race also turned heavily on economic concerns and immigration, making this only a partial driver rather than the primary determinant.
The All-In Podcast did skip its regular episode during the 2023 Summit week and released a series of guest interview episodes recorded at the summit over the following weeks.
